## 固定收益市場開篇論點

美國公債在劇烈震盪的一週收尾時，政策溢價更集中於殖利率曲線前端，長債僅小幅反彈。核心通膨高於預期，使市場幾乎完全反映聯準會9月升息。週五2年期殖利率上升3.9個基點至4.626%，5年期上升2個基點至4.783%，10年期微升0.4個基點至4.968%；30年期則下降1.3個基點至5.354%。

殖利率曲線因而轉平。2年與10年期利差收窄3.5個基點至34.2個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄5.2個基點至72.8個基點。全週2年期殖利率上升25.9個基點，10年期上升18.5個基點；在油價、生產者物價，以及市場對財政部擴大債券買回的疑慮於週四引發拋售後，兩者均接近多年高點。

8月消費者物價成為政策定價的最後一項催化劑。整體CPI月增0.4%，符合預期，高於前月的0.1%，年增率則維持3.4%。核心通膨月增0.3%，高於預期的0.2%，儘管年增率由2.5%降至2.4%。這項核心數據的月增意外，足以使市場隱含的9月升息機率由公布前約70%升至約90%，並完全反映年底前升息兩次。

市場將結果解讀為近期更有必要維持緊縮，而非長期通膨預期開始失去錨定。10年期實質殖利率上升4.9個基點至2.596%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降4.5個基點至2.372%。10年期名目殖利率盤中觸及4.98%，但收盤未突破5%，30年期債券則上漲。即使持有長天期債券所需的實質報酬仍在提高，投資人仍願意相信，聯準會採取更緊縮的政策可以抑制部分通膨衝擊。

美國時段油價回落，進一步強化這項區別。WTI期貨在前一日異常大漲後下跌2.37%至$100.05，布蘭特原油下跌2.81%至$104.61。兩項指標全週仍上漲逾8.5%，因此當日跌勢只是緩和眼前衝擊，並不代表能源情勢已經逆轉。其後週末發生的沙烏地阿拉伯東西輸油管停運，以及荷莫茲海峽周邊的新一波攻擊，在亞洲市場重開前又削弱了部分喘息空間，但這些事件均發生於週五固定收益市場收盤之後。

風險資產則認為聯準會預期中的因應尚可承受。標普500指數上漲0.86%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.91%，費城半導體指數上漲1.81%；VIX下跌11.21%至15.84。美國投資級與高收益債利差小幅收窄，主要相關ETF以總報酬計則幾乎持平。這不是融資壓力或信用狀況普遍惡化，而是在資本市場仍然開放之際，市場重新評價政策利率與實質折現率。

## 核心通膨與家庭預期提高聯準會按兵不動的門檻

8月CPI細項使聯準會更難繼續等待能源壓力自行消退。能源價格當月上漲2.1%，但核心通膨高於預期，顯示物價加速並不限於食品與燃料。排除能源與租金的服務價格上漲0.5%，無線電話服務價格創紀錄升幅，旅館、汽車旅館與機票價格也走強；屋主設算租金的漲幅則較溫和，為0.2%。

核心商品價格上漲0.1%，主要由新車與中古車帶動。科技相關項目的年增幅也異常強勁：電腦軟體及配件價格較上年同期上漲25.4%，電腦、周邊設備與智慧家庭助理裝置上漲8.4%。除關稅與能源外，這些數據也使資料中心投資熱潮所帶來的通膨壓力，進一步反映在消費者物價上。

年增率的訊號沒那麼令人憂慮。核心通膨由2.5%降至2.4%，整體通膨維持3.4%。這組結果解釋了長天期美債為何在初步拋售後表現較佳：報告強化了下次會議採取行動的理由，但尚不足以證明必須展開一連串升息。

其後公布的家庭調查，使這種相對受控的解讀變得更複雜。密西根大學9月消費者信心指數初值由51.7降至47.8，遠低於經濟學家預期的51.0。1年期通膨預期由4%跳升至4.6%，5年期指標由3.3%升至3.4%，仍高於2024年的2.8%至3.2%區間。

調查主管Joanne Hsu將家庭預期惡化歸因於燃料價格上升與貿易緊張。這種組合帶有停滯性通膨色彩，而非單純的需求擴張：受訪者預期通膨升高之際，信心也大幅轉弱。另一份薪資資料顯示，8月實質平均時薪較上年同期下降0.3%，延續伊朗戰爭爆發以來的疲弱表現。

對聯準會而言，長期通膨預期上升比信心指數本身更具政策意義。5年期指標走高，顯示能源衝擊對民眾看法的影響已超越加油站價格眼前的漲幅；信心下滑則反映通膨也在侵蝕購買力。提高利率可以抑制需求，卻無法修復受損的石油基礎設施，也不能恢復波斯灣的航運能力。

這批數據不僅改變市場定價，也促使專業機構調整預測。CPI公布後，道明證券與摩根大通均改為預期9月升息；多位經濟學家則認為，依照主席華許本人的反應函數，這些數據很可能會促使聯準會升息。華許在傑克森洞表示，若基礎通膨未能明確且足夠迅速地朝目標靠攏，聯準會就仍有工作要做。最新數據公布後若仍按兵不動，他必須解釋核心通膨月增幅加快、家庭通膨預期上升，為何不符合這項條件。

聯準會內部支持緊縮的聲音在CPI公布前便已增加。7月有3名決策者主張升息25個基點而投下反對票，另有2名非投票委員表示也會支持升息。目前的分歧在於緊縮需要維持多久、幅度多大。部分官員認為基礎通膨無須持續干預也會降溫，但市場定價目前顯示12月前還會再升息一次。

政治環境增加了不確定性，卻未改變通膨的基本計算。川普總統週末持續主張美國利率應是全球最低，並稱不清楚聯準會是否會提高借貸成本。國家經濟會議主任Kevin Hassett表示，白宮會支持委員會的任何決定，但也承認川普不會樂見升息。因此，華許在作出決策時，既要維持委員會內部支持及美國公債市場的信譽，又得採取違背總統公開偏好的行動。

週五長端相對有韌性，顯示政策信譽可以帶來什麼效果。投資人接受短期利率上升，同時降低部分通膨補償要求，使30年期殖利率得以下降。但這項支持仍有條件：CPI公布後若維持利率不變，可能被解讀為容忍通膨再起；若將升息描述為廣泛緊縮行動的開端，則可能進一步推升實質殖利率，加重住宅、政府債務及資本密集型科技投資已經面臨的融資壓力。

## 週五油價喘息後，波斯灣供給威脅再起

週五美國時段原油下跌，避免CPI公布後再次出現整條殖利率曲線全面拋售。布蘭特原油一度升破$107後，市場傳出波斯灣國家考慮就荷莫茲海峽問題與伊朗會談，加上國際能源總署預測需求轉弱，促使投資人獲利了結。油價回落時，長天期美債與股票同步上漲；美元收盤幾乎持平，黃金期貨則維持在$4,366附近。

然而，國際能源總署描述的實體市場遠比單日價格跌勢所呈現的更為緊張。該機構預測，2026年全球石油供給將每日減少570萬桶，約為6%，高於先前估計的約4%。8月全球庫存每日減少310萬桶，降至2023年以來最低；沙烏地阿拉伯原油供應每日減少230萬桶至600萬桶，為30多年來最低，OPEC+產量則每日下降180萬桶至3,880萬桶。

該機構也將波斯灣供應全面恢復的時間推遲至2027年。主要的反向力量來自需求預測：高燃料價格打擊經濟活動，預料2026年消費量將每日減少250萬桶，較先前預測的每日減少160萬桶更為嚴重。需求破壞最終可能壓抑原油價格，但代價是實質成長轉弱，而非供給恢復，也無法阻止近期通膨衝擊。

成品油構成更直接的傳導管道。美國柴油價格升破每加侖$6，歐洲與亞洲柴油漲幅也超過原油。俄羅斯煉油廠受損、中東加工能力受限及航運吃緊，削弱將現有原油轉化為運輸、工業與供暖所需燃料的能力。煉油利潤因此上升，即使原油指標價格持平或下降，也未必能為消費者與生產者物價帶來同等程度的紓緩。

美國市場收盤後的週末事件進一步加劇風險。沙烏地阿拉伯東西輸油管遭無人機攻擊後持續停運。這條管線原本每日將約400萬桶原油輸往紅海港口延布，使出口可以繞過戰時受阻的荷莫茲海峽。買家與交易員估計，若停運時間延長，全球石油供給最多可能減少4%。

據估計，延布的庫存僅足以支應五至七天的出口。不同消息來源對維修時間的評估差距很大：一名消息人士表示，全面修復可能需要五至六週，另一人則認為有機會更早恢復部分輸送。沙烏地阿拉伯向OPEC表示，其8月產量已由2月的每日1,090萬桶降至620萬桶，可用來吸收另一波中斷的備用流量因而更少。

新一波攻擊隨後推升週一亞洲開盤油價。布蘭特原油上漲$3.62至每桶$108.23，WTI上漲$3.15至$103.20。沙烏地媒體報導，胡塞武裝攻擊吉贊省及附近一座軍事基地；荷莫茲海峽一艘船舶則遭投射物擊中後起火，船員被迫撤離。伊朗另稱，一艘伊朗商船上有1人死亡、4人受傷。

阿曼外交部長Badr Albusaidi也表示，波斯灣國家與伊朗原定週一舉行的會議已延期。會議原本預計討論荷莫茲海峽，以及可能達成的臨時航運安排。在實體基礎設施損害益發迫切之際，會議延後也移除了週五促使油價下跌的一項外交因素。

這些週末事件無法解釋週五美債收盤走勢，卻重新設定了下一個交易日的起點。週五損益兩平通膨率下降，部分仰賴油價走低及市場相信聯準會將採取行動。若輸油管持續停運或航運再受干擾，在市場已上調預期政策路徑後，近期通膨衝擊將進一步加劇，並同時考驗上述兩項假設。

## 日本與歐洲進一步走入能源驅動的緊縮週期

日本提供了相當明確的證據，顯示全球政策轉向並不只限於聯準會。8月生產者物價年增7.6%，高於預測的7.4%，僅略低於上修後的7月增幅7.7%。指數月減0.2%，前月增幅則上修至0.4%；但油煤製品、化學品、通訊設備與非鐵金屬的年度價格壓力仍相當普遍。

進口成本漲勢更為極端。以日圓計價的進口物價指數年增24.8%，雖低於上修後的7月增幅29.3%，企業仍持續面臨更高的能源、航運、包裝與工資成本，上游壓力轉嫁至消費者物價的風險因而升高。

4名熟悉日本央行想法的人士表示，9月17日至18日會議升息25個基點至1.25%的條件正逐步到位。這將是31年來最高政策利率，並接續6月升至1%的行動。重要但書是，政策委員尚未就終端利率或預定升息步調達成共識。若通膨超出預期，官員可能釋出加快行動的訊號，但總裁植田和男不太可能讓央行受制於固定路徑。

儘管如此，經濟學家已大幅提前升息預期。彭博調查的52名受訪者全數預期9月升息；先前7月調查時，沒有任何人作此預測。93%預期明年1月前還會再升息一次，其中約三分之一認為時間點在12月。約46%預期每季升息一次，僅6%仍認為會維持7月調查時占主流的每六個月一次步調。終端利率預測中位數仍為1.75%。

日本公債已反映較快的政策路徑。週五10年期殖利率上升7.5個基點至2.985%，20年期上升7個基點至3.82%。這波走勢一方面跟隨全球債市拋售，另一方面也反映國內通膨數據，以及日本央行可能更頻繁採取行動。日圓在美國時段一度升值0.8%至1美元兌153.24日圓，之後回吐部分漲幅。

匯率仍是潛在的跨市場傳導管道。第1季對境外非銀行借款人的日圓貸款與存款餘額為¥42兆，低於2024年底創紀錄的¥45.7兆，但接近10年前的兩倍。日圓若失序升值，可能迫使其他市場削減槓桿部位。目前這波升勢較2024年溫和，投資人也有更多時間為日本央行緊縮做好準備；但日圓融資的利差優勢日益縮小，這類交易承受波動的空間也隨之下降。

日本儲蓄對海外債券的支持也可能減弱。桑坦德估計，即使政府退休金投資基金不正式改變資產配置政策，也可能減持足以造成最多$620億美債賣盤的外國債券。該基金目前以外國債券占25%為目標，容許上下偏離5個百分點；降至區間下緣仍符合現行規定。這只是情境推估，並非已公布的交易，但顯示在任何正式資產配置檢討前，JGB殖利率上升與日圓走強已可能影響美債的邊際需求。

歐洲央行進行戰後第2次升息後，歐洲的政策訊息也更加明確。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel表示，利率已接近中性區間上緣，可能需要進入溫和限制性區域。愛沙尼亞央行總裁Ulo Kaasik表示，市場預期繼續升息可以理解，目前利率仍不算特別高。立陶宛央行總裁Gediminas Simkus則強調，通膨依然過高，重要的不只是當前水準，也包括持續時間。

歐洲央行總裁拉加德週末進一步強化這項看法，表示能源衝擊可能比先前預期持續更久。她指出，能源成本上升與中東衝突及煉油能力受損有關，尤其是俄羅斯煉油能力受創；持續的通膨壓力加上經濟仍具韌性，迫使歐洲央行作出回應。最新預測顯示，歐元區通膨率在2026年為3%、2027年為2.5%、2028年為2.1%，2026年經濟成長預測則上調至0.9%。

英國數據削弱了以成長為由反對最終緊縮的論點。7月GDP月增0.4%，優於零成長的預期；年增1.6%，也高於預測的1.2%。截至7月的三個月產出成長0.4%，受電腦程式設計等服務業帶動。市場認為英格蘭銀行11月前升息幾乎已成定局，儘管多數經濟學家預期即將召開的會議不會採取行動。

其他央行面臨的選擇則更加分歧。燃料短缺、政府支出加速及通膨預期偏高打斷俄羅斯的降息週期，俄羅斯自2025年6月以來首次將政策利率維持在14%。年通膨已加速至6.3%，俄羅斯央行表示促升通膨的風險占上風。其2026年通膨預測為6%至7%，意味通膨將連續第七年高於4%目標，但官員仍預期2027年可回到目標。

巴西則有空間繼續降息。8月IPCA通膨率由4.44%降至4.22%，低於預測的4.27%；物價月減0.32%，降幅大於預期的0.29%。一次性電費折扣使住宅相關成本下降1.87%，代表改善的持續性有限。即便如此，經濟學家仍認為結果支持再次將Selic利率調降25個基點至13.75%，而非加快降息步調。

## 印度把流動性警告化為債券供給

印度由口頭警告轉向明確的資產負債表操作。印度央行總裁Sanjay Malhotra表示，央行可透過公開市場賣債及外匯交換吸收過剩流動性，所有工具都在考慮範圍內。銀行體系現金盈餘達10.49兆盧比；此前，銀行透過一項特別外幣籌資計畫募得約$1,270億。

市場最初的反應集中於較短天期。Malhotra發言後，指標10年期殖利率上升6個基點至7.035%，5年期一度上升10個基點至6.6222%。儘管維持交易的機會成本很高，流動性良好的5年期指標債空頭部位，已使9月初每日借券規模升破1,000億盧比，約為8月初的兩倍。

週五稍早的標售顯示，印度央行正在資金需求與市場重新定價之間求取平衡。票息6.20%的2029年期公債原定發行1,100億盧比，央行僅接受450.6億盧比投標，截標殖利率定為6.4031%，低於交易員估計的6.47%。央行則按計畫售出1,100億盧比2033年期債券及1,000億盧比新發2056年期債券。部分拒標顯示，即使央行準備收回原本支撐短債的流動性，也不願接受市場對較短天期債券要求的更高殖利率。

週五稍晚、當地市場收盤後，印度央行宣布直接出售1兆盧比債券，是迄今為抽離過剩資金所採取的最強硬措施。操作將分別於9月17日、21日及28日進行，共分三批。首批出售的證券於2029年至2032年間到期，直接向受銀行過剩現金扭曲最嚴重的曲線區段增加久期供給。

央行仍有能力繼續操作。上個會計年度，其政府債券持有量增加逾40%至約23兆盧比，相當於中央政府流通在外證券的約18%。先前的浮動利率反向附買回操作僅能暫時抽離流動性，未能使隔夜利率重新貼近政策訊號。直接售債能更持久地收回資金，卻也會在油價上漲已對通膨前景構成壓力之際增加供給。

印度債市與匯市週一休市，因此週二重開時才會消化這項公告及任何新的通膨資訊。分析師預期10年期殖利率可能上升約10個基點，較短天期反應可能更大，並警告現金盈餘規模或許需要央行採取進一步措施。

印度央行10月7日的政策決定因此不再只是附買回利率的問題。在正式升息之前，流動性操作已開始收緊金融情勢；油價上漲則從通膨、經常帳與匯率三方面對印度構成壓力。某項估計顯示，布蘭特原油每上漲$10，可能使通膨增加35個基點、經濟成長減少15個基點；不過，降低對波斯灣供應商依賴的多元化措施或可減輕敏感度。

## 財政壓力與信用供給造成相對價值分化

即使30年期美債週五上漲，美國財政情勢仍提供另一項使長期殖利率維持高檔的結構性理由。2026會計年度前11個月，聯邦赤字達$1.97兆；經日曆因素調整後，較可比期間減少5%，但仍是史上最高水準之一。8月赤字為$1,668億，7月則為$4,323億。

本會計年度迄今支出達$6.81兆，收入為$4.85兆；經調整後，兩者均成長3%。淨利息支出達$1兆，超過國防及除社會安全與主管Medicare的部門之外的所有主要類別。截至8月底，可交易美國公債的平均利率為3.48%，比五年前高逾2個百分點；隨著低票息證券到期，平均利率還會繼續上升。

這些數據使市場殖利率與未來融資需求形成回饋循環。公共債務已超過$40兆，美國國會預算辦公室則預期，債務占GDP比率將在2030年前突破1946年的紀錄。川普總統提議，若共和黨保住國會控制權，將向每名成年人發放$5,000；方案若通過，成本約為$1.2兆。目前尚無任何法案獲准，但這項提議加深投資人的疑慮：期中選舉前，財政整頓缺乏政治支持。

法國更鮮明地顯示，主權債已失去在國內信用市場一向居於最高層級的地位。主要由房貸擔保、並有優先受償權及抵押品保障的法國擔保債券，殖利率比10年期政府公債低近30個基點，倒掛幅度創歷來最大；四個月前，兩類債券殖利率還大致相同。

法國10年期殖利率交投於4.43%至4.46%附近，對德國公債利差本週一度升破90個基點，為歐元區債務危機以來最寬。經濟也在轉弱：法國國家統計機構將2026年成長預測由0.7%下調至0.4%，使政府更難壓低2025年占GDP 5.1%的財政赤字。

法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin警告，每年債務償付成本到2028或2029年可能逼近€1,000億。其後，央行罕見發表聲明，否認曾出售透過歐洲央行購債計畫買入的證券。這項爭議是更廣泛選舉辯論的一環，極左派候選人Jean-Luc Mélenchon提議取消法國央行與歐洲央行持有的法國債務。法國央行表示並未出售任何相關證券；Moulin則稱，取消債務等同非法違約，將推升通膨與借貸成本。

在主權壓力背景下，信用市場仍然開放，但選擇性日益提高。美國上市公司今年已發行創紀錄的$1,310億可轉換證券，其中8月發行$250億，約44%來自AI相關企業。Alphabet的$205億強制可轉換證券及Oracle的$50億發行案均名列最大交易，Nebius則分兩筆募得$57.5億。

可轉換債讓借款人以股票選擇權取代部分現金利息。新發可轉換債近30%為零票息；一名顧問估計，平均規模$8億的交易若以票息1.5%的可轉換債取代票息7.5%的普通債券，每年可節省近$5,000萬。當美債殖利率逼近5%，AI基礎建設又需要為晶片、資料中心、電力及不動產籌資時，這項成本節省尤其重要。

發債活動也正跨向不同幣別。Meta曾與歐洲債券投資人進行非交易型路演，但尚未承諾發債。Amazon已在首次英鎊發債中募得£42.5億，也發行歐元、瑞士法郎及加幣債券；Alphabet則已進入6個非美元市場。先前一筆與Meta相關的資料中心融資，因需求弱於往常，最終票息高於7.5%，顯示有市場管道不等於能取得低成本資金。

銀行資本工具獲得更強勁需求。三菱日聯金融集團發行¥2,000億永續型額外第一類資本債，分為5年4個月及10年4個月可贖回批次，相對政府債券曲線利差分別為100與105個基點。兩批利差均比MUFG 4月發行時收窄5個基點，最終需求達¥2,482億。這與日圓優先順位公司債利差擴大的走勢形成對比，顯示當額外票息足以補償風險時，投資人偏好知名度高的發行人所發行的次順位證券。

瑞銀則運用強勁融資能力縮減承接而來的負債。該行在迄今最大規模的回購中，接受$79億瑞信舊債投標，使遺留債務由2023年收購時約$900億降至約$290億。瑞銀曾兩度提高部分收購要約的上限，另發行$60億新優先債。這項交易可降低利息支出與過剩融資，但瑞銀仍面臨瑞士資本改革尚未解決的國會辯論。

較弱的信用體未獲同樣待遇。South East Water與投資人就定價的磋商陷入停滯後，重新評估公開發債計畫。這家公用事業公司獲King Street Capital提供£2億流動性備援，以防先前預估明年8月可能出現的現金危機。其負債比率為66.5%，高於監管機關目標；近期還因服務失誤及信用評等遭調降，支付£3,050萬補償金。市場並非沒有需求，只是投資人提出的條件並非公司願意接受。

澳洲監管機關也在檢視私募信貸與受監管金融體系之間的界線。審慎監理機關已聯繫銀行與退休基金，了解其對倒閉地產開發商Bathla Group的曝險。該集團積欠債權人約A$34億，債權人以私人貸款機構為主。銀行與受監管退休基金的直接曝險似乎有限，澳洲央行也表示尚未發現系統性壓力；然而，這項調查反映監管機關擔心資訊透明度不足與估值不確定，可能掩蓋私募信貸違約向外擴散的管道。

塞內加爾在宣布債務處理計畫後進行的區域標售，則釋出較具建設性的訊號。政府原定籌資1,000億CFA法郎，實際募得1,010億CFA法郎，約合$1.79億。投資人投標1,090億CFA法郎，政府幾乎全部接受。5年期殖利率由前次標售的8.24%降至7.89%，1年期國庫券與3年期債券平均殖利率分別為7.87%與7.75%。

結果顯示，塞內加爾的計畫並未立即衝擊區域市場。政府打算將CFA法郎債務排除在外，並依G20共同框架，為外部債務爭取延長到期日及降低利率。這項區隔目前維持了本地需求，但在未揭露借款導致IMF暫停$18億融資後，也使最終談判更集中於國際債權人。

## 後續市場意義

9月16日的聯準會決策、經濟預測及華許記者會是最重要的考驗。核心CPI月增0.3%、家庭通膨預期升高後，市場預期將升息25個基點；更大的問題是，決策者會將此舉描述為有限度收回先前寬鬆，還是更長期緊縮行動的開始。週五殖利率曲線轉平、損益兩平通膨率下降，顯示投資人目前認為政策緊縮能夠抑制通膨。若指引暗示緊縮程度將明顯加大，實質殖利率可能上升；若維持利率不變，則會考驗聯準會在長端市場的信譽。

8月零售銷售將在9月16日決策前公布。市場預期月增0.9%，扭轉前月下降0.6%的走勢，但現有預測分歧。進出口物價也會同時公布。零售需求將顯示，較高價格究竟由仍具韌性的消費者吸收，還是已在侵蝕實質支出；進口物價則會更直接反映關稅、能源及匯率變動如何傳導至美國成本。

美國公債供給將另行考驗長天期債券需求。9月15日預定標售20年期公債，前次得標殖利率為5.204%；9月17日接著標售10年期TIPS，前次實質殖利率為2.438%。在10年期美債殖利率接近5%時，名目債標售將檢驗需求是否仍然穩健；10年期實質殖利率已升至2.596%、損益兩平通膨率下降後，抗通膨債券標售則會測試投資人承接意願。

在預定數據公布前，油價便可能先牽動這些市場。沙烏地阿拉伯東西輸油管仍停運，其出口庫存估計僅足以支應五至七天。若恢復部分輸送，可減輕眼前威脅；若修復需時五至六週，全球供給最多可能減少4%。波斯灣國家與伊朗的會談延期，加上荷莫茲海峽周邊再遭攻擊，已使週五原油跌勢在亞洲開盤時逆轉。

日本央行預計於9月17日至18日會議升息25個基點至1.25%。這一步驟實際上已獲市場定價，真正的考驗是植田和男會否認可更快的升息節奏，同時保留終端利率的彈性。若訊號符合每季升息一次的預期，將支撐日圓與JGB殖利率，也可能加速日本儲蓄轉回國內債券；若僅例行升息並給出謹慎指引，則會挑戰調查中明年1月前再升息一次的共識。

英格蘭銀行將在英國勞動市場與通膨數據公布後，於9月17日作出決策。多數經濟學家預期不會立即調整政策，但7月GDP成長0.4%，加上能源衝擊再起，已提高11月前採取行動的機率。英國政府公債長天期借貸成本已接近數十年高點，因此英格蘭銀行每年公布的公債持有部位縮減步調，將與政策利率同樣重要。

印度當地市場恢復交易時，必須消化印度央行出售1兆盧比債券的公告。首批操作於9月17日進行，標的為2029年至2032年間到期的債券。殖利率反應將顯示，抽走創紀錄的過剩流動性究竟只是恢復政策訊號，還是會迫使短、中天期債券出現更劇烈的重新定價。

9月17日將公布新屋開工、建築許可與初領失業救濟金人數，9月18日接著公布8月工業生產。初領失業救濟金人數在前值20.6萬後，預期將維持在接近20.9萬的水準；新屋開工則預期自7月的跌勢中反彈。若裁員維持低檔且生產有韌性，聯準會將更有能力優先處理通膨；若經濟普遍轉弱，任何緊縮週期的持續時間與政策溝通，就會比首次升息本身更為重要。

overall_summary.headline: 核心通膨高於預期推升前端殖利率，長天期美債維持穩健
overall_summary.session_narrative:
2年期美債殖利率上升3.9個基點至4.626%，10年期微升0.4個基點至4.968%，30年期則下降1.3個基點至5.354%。8月核心CPI月增0.3%，高於預測的0.2%，使市場隱含的聯準會9月升息機率升至約90%，並完全反映年底前升息兩次，殖利率曲線因而轉平。

市場將這份數據解讀為近期更有必要維持緊縮，而非長期通膨預期失去錨定。10年期實質殖利率上升4.9個基點至2.596%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降4.5個基點至2.372%。美國時段油價回落，帶動長天期美債回升；不過，原油全週仍上漲逾8.5%，實體供應風險也尚未解除。

家庭數據使政策選擇更加棘手：消費者信心降至47.8，1年期通膨預期升至4.6%，5年期指標升至3.4%。即便如此，股市上漲、波動率下降，信用利差也小幅收窄，顯示市場是在重新評價政策利率與實質折現率，而非面臨普遍融資壓力。
overall_summary.summary: 核心CPI月增幅高於預期，使聯準會9月升息幾乎獲得完全定價，美債殖利率曲線因而轉平；油價回落、損益兩平通膨率下降及長債上漲，則顯示投資人仍相信較緊的政策能抑制部分通膨衝擊。

section_summaries.section_title: 固定收益市場開篇論點

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries ended a bruising week with a sharper policy premium at the front of the curve but a limited recovery in long bonds, as hotter core inflation brought a September Federal Reserve increase close to fully priced. The 2-year yield rose 3.9 basis points on Friday to 4.626%, the 5-year gained 2 basis points to 4.783%, and the 10-year edged 0.4 basis point higher to 4.968%. The 30-year yield fell 1.3 basis points to 5.354%.

The curve flattened accordingly. The 2s10s spread narrowed 3.5 basis points to 34.2, while 2s30s compressed 5.2 basis points to 72.8. Over the week, the 2-year yield rose 25.9 basis points and the 10-year increased 18.5 basis points, leaving both close to multiyear highs after oil, producer prices and doubts about Treasury’s enlarged buybacks had driven Thursday’s selloff.

August consumer prices supplied the final policy catalyst. Headline CPI rose 0.4% from July, matching expectations after a 0.1% increase, and remained 3.4% higher than a year earlier. Core inflation rose 0.3% on the month rather than the 0.2% expected, although its annual rate eased to 2.4% from 2.5%. The monthly core surprise was enough to lift the market-implied probability of a September rate increase to around 90%, from roughly 70% before the release, and leave two moves fully priced by year-end.

The market treated that outcome as a stronger case for near-term restraint rather than evidence that longer-run inflation was becoming unanchored. The 10-year real yield rose 4.9 basis points to 2.596%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 4.5 basis points to 2.372%. The 10-year nominal yield touched 4.98% intraday but did not close through 5%, and the 30-year rallied. Investors were willing to accept that tighter Fed policy could contain part of the inflation impulse even as the required real return on duration continued to rise.

Oil’s retreat during the U.S. session reinforced that distinction. WTI futures fell 2.37% to $100.05 and Brent declined 2.81% to $104.61 after an extraordinary rise the previous day. Both benchmarks still gained more than 8.5% over the week, so the decline represented relief from the immediate shock rather than a reversal of the energy regime. The later weekend shutdown of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and new attacks around the Strait of Hormuz removed part of that relief before Asian markets reopened, but those events occurred after Friday’s fixed-income close.

Risk assets interpreted the expected Fed response as manageable. The S&P 500 rose 0.86%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.91%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index advanced 1.81%. The VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads tightened modestly, while their principal exchange-traded funds were nearly unchanged on a total-return basis. The pattern was not one of funding stress or broad credit deterioration. It was a repricing of the policy rate and real discount rate against a still-open capital market.

## Core Inflation and Household Expectations Raise the Bar for a Fed Hold

The August CPI details left the Fed with less room to wait for energy pressure to dissipate. Energy prices rose 2.1% during the month, but the upside core surprise showed that the acceleration was not confined to food and fuel. Services excluding energy and rents increased 0.5%, helped by a record rise in wireless telephone services as well as stronger hotel, motel and airline fares. Owners’ equivalent rent rose a more moderate 0.2%.

Core goods prices increased 0.1%, led by new and used vehicles. Technology-related categories also showed unusually strong annual increases: computer software and accessories prices rose 25.4% from a year earlier, while computers, peripherals and smart-home assistants increased 8.4%. The figures added a consumer-price dimension to the inflation pressure associated with the data-center investment boom, alongside tariffs and energy.

The annual comparisons were less alarming. Core inflation slowed to 2.4% from 2.5%, and headline inflation remained at 3.4%. That combination explains why long-dated Treasuries outperformed after the initial selloff: the report strengthened the case for action at the next meeting without proving that a prolonged sequence of increases would be necessary.

Household data later in the session complicated that relatively contained interpretation. The preliminary University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index fell to 47.8 in September from 51.7, well below the 51.0 expected by economists. One-year inflation expectations jumped to 4.6% from 4%, while the 5-year measure rose to 3.4% from 3.3% and remained above its 2024 range of 2.8%-3.2%.

Survey director Joanne Hsu linked the deterioration in household expectations to higher fuel prices and trade tensions. The combination was stagflationary rather than simply expansionary: confidence weakened sharply even as respondents expected more inflation. Separate wage data showed real average hourly earnings falling 0.3% from a year earlier in August, extending a run of weak readings since the Iran war began.

For the Fed, the longer-run expectation was more consequential than the sentiment headline alone. A higher 5-year reading suggests the energy shock is influencing beliefs beyond the immediate rise in pump prices. The decline in confidence, meanwhile, shows that the inflation impulse is also reducing purchasing power. Higher rates can restrain demand, but they cannot repair damaged oil infrastructure or restore shipping capacity through the Gulf.

The release shifted the center of the professional forecast as well as market pricing. TD Securities and JPMorgan moved to expecting a September increase after the CPI data, and several economists described a hike as the likely consequence of Chair Kevin Warsh’s own reaction function. Warsh said at Jackson Hole that the Fed would have work to do if underlying inflation did not move clearly and sufficiently quickly toward its objective. Holding after the latest data would require him to explain why the monthly core acceleration and higher household expectations did not meet that condition.

Internal support for tightening had already grown before CPI. Three policymakers dissented in July in favor of a quarter-point increase, and two non-voters had indicated that they would also have supported one. The remaining disagreement concerns the persistence and scale of tightening. Some officials expect underlying inflation to cool without sustained intervention, while market pricing now implies another increase by December.

The political setting adds uncertainty without changing the inflation arithmetic. President Donald Trump continued over the weekend to argue that the U.S. should have the world’s lowest rates and said he did not know whether the Fed would increase borrowing costs. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said the White House would support whatever the committee decided, while acknowledging that Trump would not be pleased by a hike. Warsh therefore enters the decision needing to preserve support inside the committee and credibility in the Treasury market while acting against the president’s stated preference.

The long end’s relative resilience on Friday showed what credibility could deliver. Investors accepted higher short rates while reducing some inflation compensation, allowing the 30-year yield to fall. That support remains conditional. A hold after CPI could be interpreted as tolerance of renewed inflation, while a hike presented as the start of a broad campaign could lift real yields further and increase the financing pressure already visible in housing, government debt and capital-intensive technology investment.

## Friday’s Oil Relief Gives Way to a Renewed Gulf Supply Threat

The decline in crude during Friday’s U.S. session helped keep the CPI response from becoming another full-curve rout. Reports that Gulf states were considering talks with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz and the International Energy Agency’s forecast of weaker demand encouraged profit-taking after Brent had traded above $107. The fall in oil accompanied gains in long Treasuries and equities, while the dollar finished almost unchanged and gold futures held near $4,366.

The IEA’s assessment nevertheless described a much tighter physical market than the daily price decline suggested. It forecast world oil supply would contract by 5.7 million barrels a day in 2026, or about 6%, compared with a previous estimate of roughly 4%. Global inventories fell by 3.1 million barrels a day in August to their lowest level since 2023, while Saudi crude supply dropped by 2.3 million barrels a day to 6 million, its lowest in more than three decades. OPEC+ output fell by 1.8 million barrels a day to 38.8 million.

The agency also pushed a full recovery in Gulf supply into 2027. Its demand forecast supplied the principal counterforce: consumption was expected to fall by 2.5 million barrels a day in 2026, compared with a previous forecast for a 1.6 million decline, as high fuel prices damaged activity. That demand destruction can eventually restrain crude prices, but it arrives through weaker real growth rather than restored supply and does not prevent a near-term inflation shock.

Refined products present an even more immediate transmission channel. Diesel prices in the U.S. rose above $6 a gallon, while European and Asian diesel prices increased faster than crude. Russian refinery damage, impaired Middle Eastern processing and constrained shipping have reduced the ability to convert available crude into the fuels used by trucking, industry and heating. The resulting rise in refining margins means that a stable or lower crude benchmark does not necessarily deliver equivalent relief to consumer or producer prices.

Events over the weekend intensified that risk after the completed U.S. close. Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline remained shut following a drone strike. The route had been carrying about 4 million barrels a day to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, allowing exports to bypass the wartime impairment of the Strait of Hormuz. Buyers and traders estimated that a prolonged outage could remove as much as 4% of global oil supply.

Yanbu inventories were estimated to cover only five to seven days of exports. Repair assessments varied materially: one source said full work could take five to six weeks, while another saw a possibility of partial pumping sooner. Saudi Arabia told OPEC that its August production had fallen to 6.2 million barrels a day from 10.9 million in February, leaving less spare flow to absorb another disruption.

Fresh attacks then lifted prices at Monday’s Asian opening. Brent rose $3.62 to $108.23 a barrel and WTI gained $3.15 to $103.20. Saudi media reported Houthi strikes on Jazan province and a nearby military base, while a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by a projectile, caught fire and required its crew to evacuate. Iran separately reported one death and four injuries aboard an Iranian commercial ship.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi also said a planned Monday meeting between Gulf countries and Iran had been postponed. The gathering was expected to discuss the Strait and potentially a temporary shipping arrangement. Its delay removed a diplomatic source of Friday’s oil decline just as physical infrastructure damage became more pressing.

Those weekend developments cannot explain Friday’s Treasury close, but they reset the starting conditions for the next session. Friday’s fall in breakevens depended partly on lower oil and confidence that the Fed would respond. A sustained pipeline outage or further shipping disruption would test both propositions by increasing the near-term inflation impulse after markets had already raised the expected policy path.

## Japan and Europe Move Further Into the Energy-Driven Tightening Cycle

Japan supplied some of the clearest evidence that the global policy shift extends beyond the Fed. Producer prices rose 7.6% from a year earlier in August, exceeding the 7.4% forecast and only slightly below a revised 7.7% increase in July. The index fell 0.2% on the month after a revised 0.4% rise, but the annual pressure remained broad across oil and coal products, chemicals, communications equipment and non-ferrous metals.

Import costs were more extreme. The yen-based import-price index rose 24.8% from a year earlier, although that was slower than the revised 29.3% increase in July. Companies continued to face higher energy, shipping, packaging and wage costs, increasing the risk that upstream pressure would pass into consumer prices.

Four people familiar with Bank of Japan thinking said conditions were falling into place for a 25-basis-point increase to 1.25% at the Sept. 17-18 meeting. That would be the highest policy rate in 31 years and would follow June’s increase to 1%. The important qualification was that the board had no agreed terminal rate or predetermined pace. Officials could signal faster action if inflation overshot, but Governor Kazuo Ueda was unlikely to bind the bank to a fixed path.

Economists have nevertheless brought forward their expectations materially. All 52 respondents to a Bloomberg survey expected an increase in September, compared with none in the previous July survey. Some 93% anticipated another move by January, including roughly one-third who expected December. About 46% expected increases at a quarterly pace, while only 6% still saw the 6-month cadence that had dominated the July poll. The median terminal-rate estimate remained 1.75%.

Japanese government bonds had already adjusted to that faster path. The 10-year yield rose 7.5 basis points to 2.985% on Friday, while the 20-year gained 7 basis points to 3.82%. The move tracked the global selloff but also reflected the domestic inflation data and prospect of more frequent BOJ action. The yen strengthened as much as 0.8% during the U.S. session to 153.24 per dollar before paring part of the advance.

The currency remains a potential cross-market transmission channel. Yen loans and deposits to offshore non-bank borrowers stood at ¥42 trillion in Q1, down from a record ¥45.7 trillion in late 2024 but almost twice the level of a decade earlier. A disorderly yen rise could force reductions in leveraged positions elsewhere. The current advance has been more gradual than the 2024 episode, and investors have had more time to anticipate BOJ tightening, but the shrinking interest-rate advantage of yen funding makes the trade less forgiving.

Japanese savings may also become less supportive of overseas duration. Santander estimated that the Government Pension Investment Fund could reduce foreign-bond holdings by enough to generate as much as $62 billion of Treasury sales without formally changing its allocation policy. Its current target is 25% foreign bonds with a permitted deviation of 5 percentage points. Moving to the bottom of that range would remain inside the existing rules. The calculation is a scenario rather than an announced transaction, but it shows how higher JGB yields and a stronger yen can affect marginal demand for Treasuries before any official asset-allocation review.

Europe’s policy message also became more explicit after the ECB’s second postwar increase. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said rates were near the upper end of neutral and might need to enter mildly restrictive territory. Estonian central-bank Governor Ulo Kaasik said market expectations for further hikes were understandable and that the current rate was not yet especially high. Lithuanian Governor Gediminas Simkus emphasized that inflation remained excessive and that its duration, not only its current level, mattered.

ECB President Christine Lagarde reinforced that assessment over the weekend, saying the energy shock would probably last longer than previously expected. She linked higher energy costs to the Middle East conflict and damaged refining capacity, particularly in Russia, and said the combination of persistent inflation pressure and a resilient economy obliged the ECB to react. New projections put euro-area inflation at 3% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028, while the 2026 growth forecast was raised to 0.9%.

The UK data reduced the growth argument against eventual tightening. GDP rose 0.4% in July, compared with expectations for no growth, and increased 1.6% from a year earlier rather than the 1.2% forecast. Output grew 0.4% in the three months through July, helped by services including computer programming. Markets viewed a Bank of England increase by November as near certain, even though most economists expected no move at the coming meeting.

Other central banks faced more divergent choices. Russia held its key rate at 14% for the first time since June 2025 as fuel shortages, faster state spending and elevated expectations interrupted its easing cycle. Annual inflation had accelerated to 6.3%, and the Bank of Russia said pro-inflationary risks dominated. Its 2026 forecast of 6%-7% implies a seventh consecutive year above the 4% target, although officials still expect a return to target in 2027.

Brazil received room to continue easing. August IPCA inflation slowed to 4.22% from 4.44%, below the 4.27% forecast, while prices fell 0.32% on the month against an expected 0.29% decline. A one-off electricity discount drove a 1.87% fall in housing costs, limiting the durability of the improvement. Even so, economists judged the result consistent with another 25-basis-point reduction in the Selic rate to 13.75%, rather than a faster pace.

## India Turns a Liquidity Warning Into Bond Supply

India moved from verbal warning to a defined balance-sheet operation. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the Reserve Bank of India could use open-market bond sales and foreign-exchange swaps to absorb excess liquidity and that no tool was off the table. The banking system’s cash surplus stood at 10.49 trillion rupees after lenders raised about $127 billion through a special foreign-currency mobilization program.

The initial market response was concentrated in shorter maturities. The benchmark 10-year yield rose 6 basis points to 7.035% after Malhotra’s comments, while the 5-year climbed as much as 10 basis points to 6.6222%. Short positions in the liquid 5-year benchmark had already pushed daily borrowing above 100 billion rupees at the start of September, roughly twice the early-August level, despite the high opportunity cost of maintaining the trade.

An auction earlier Friday showed the RBI balancing funding needs against that repricing. It accepted only 45.06 billion rupees of bids for the 6.20% 2029 bond against an offered 110 billion, setting a 6.4031% cutoff yield compared with a 6.47% trader estimate. It sold the planned 110 billion rupees of 2033 notes and 100 billion rupees of new 2056 bonds. The partial rejection suggested the central bank was unwilling to accept the market’s higher yield on shorter debt even as it prepared to withdraw the liquidity that had supported that sector.

Later Friday, after the local market had closed, the RBI announced 1 trillion rupees of outright bond sales, its strongest step yet to drain the surplus. The operation will be divided into three tranches on Sept. 17, Sept. 21 and Sept. 28. The first sale includes securities maturing from 2029 through 2032, placing the additional duration directly into the part of the curve most distorted by excess bank cash.

The central bank has capacity to continue. Its government-bond holdings rose more than 40% in the last fiscal year to about 23 trillion rupees, or roughly 18% of outstanding central-government securities. Variable-rate reverse-repurchase operations had withdrawn liquidity only temporarily and had not restored overnight rates to the policy signal. Outright sales create a more durable drain but add supply while higher crude prices are already pressuring the inflation outlook.

India’s bond and currency markets were closed Monday, leaving Tuesday’s reopening to absorb the announcement and any new inflation information. Analysts expected the 10-year yield could rise about 10 basis points, with a larger response in shorter maturities, and warned that the scale of the cash surplus might require further measures.

The RBI’s Oct. 7 policy decision is therefore no longer only a question of the repo rate. Liquidity operations have begun to tighten financial conditions before a formal increase, while oil threatens India through inflation, the current account and the currency. One estimate put the effect of every $10 rise in Brent at 35 basis points of additional inflation and 15 basis points of lost growth, although diversification away from Gulf suppliers may reduce the sensitivity.

## Fiscal Stress and Credit Supply Produce Uneven Relative Value

The U.S. fiscal position added another structural reason for long yields to remain elevated even as the 30-year rallied on Friday. The federal deficit reached $1.97 trillion in the first 11 months of fiscal 2026, down 5% from the comparable period after calendar adjustments but still among the largest on record. August’s deficit was $166.8 billion, compared with $432.3 billion in July.

Spending reached $6.81 trillion for the fiscal year to date and revenue totaled $4.85 trillion, both 3% higher on an adjusted basis. Net interest expense reached $1 trillion, exceeding defense and every other major category except Social Security and the department overseeing Medicare. The average interest rate on marketable Treasuries was 3.48% at the end of August, more than 2 percentage points above its level five years earlier, and will rise further as lower-coupon securities mature.

The figures create a feedback loop between market yields and future financing needs. Public debt has already exceeded $40 trillion, while the Congressional Budget Office expects debt relative to GDP to surpass the 1946 record by 2030. President Trump’s proposal to send $5,000 to every adult if Republicans retain Congress would add roughly $1.2 trillion if enacted. No legislation has been approved, but the proposal reinforces investor concern that fiscal consolidation has little political constituency before the midterm election.

France offered a more acute example of sovereign credit losing its conventional place at the top of the domestic hierarchy. French covered bonds, backed mainly by mortgages and protected by seniority and collateral, yielded almost 30 basis points less than 10-year government debt, the widest inversion on record. Four months earlier, the two sectors yielded roughly the same.

French 10-year yields traded near 4.43%-4.46%, while the spread over Germany had moved above 90 basis points during the week, its widest since the euro-area debt crisis. The economy also weakened: the national statistics office cut its 2026 growth forecast to 0.4% from 0.7%, complicating the government’s effort to reduce a deficit that was 5.1% of GDP in 2025.

Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin warned that annual debt-service costs could approach €100 billion by 2028 or 2029. The central bank later issued an unusual statement denying claims that it had sold securities acquired under ECB purchase programs. The dispute forms part of a broader election debate over far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s proposal to cancel French debt held by the Bank of France and ECB. The Bank of France said none of the securities had been sold, while Moulin described cancellation as an illegal default that would raise inflation and borrowing costs.

Credit markets remained open but increasingly selective against that sovereign backdrop. U.S.-listed companies have raised a record $131 billion of convertible securities this year, including $25 billion in August. About 44% of the issuance came from AI-related companies. Alphabet’s $20.5 billion mandatory convertible transaction and Oracle’s $5 billion sale were among the largest, while Nebius raised $5.75 billion across two issues.

Convertibles allow borrowers to substitute equity optionality for cash interest. Nearly 30% of new convertible bonds carried no coupon, and one adviser estimated that replacing a 7.5% straight bond with a 1.5% convertible could save almost $50 million annually on an average $800 million transaction. The savings matter as the AI buildout requires financing for chips, data centers, electricity and real estate while Treasury yields approach 5%.

The supply is also migrating across currencies. Meta held meetings with European bond investors in a non-deal roadshow, although it had not committed to an offering. Amazon had already raised £4.25 billion in its sterling debut and issued in euros, Swiss francs and Canadian dollars, while Alphabet had tapped six non-dollar markets. A prior data-center financing linked to Meta priced with a coupon above 7.5% after weaker-than-usual demand, demonstrating that access does not guarantee inexpensive funding.

Bank capital attracted stronger demand. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group priced ¥200 billion of perpetual additional Tier 1 debt in 5-year-4-month and 10-year-4-month callable tranches at 100 and 105 basis points over the government curve. Both were 5 basis points tighter than MUFG’s April sale, and final demand reached ¥248.2 billion. The result contrasted with wider spreads on senior yen corporate bonds and showed investors favoring subordinated securities from a highly recognized issuer when the additional coupon compensated for their risk.

UBS used strong funding access to shrink inherited liabilities. It accepted $7.9 billion of old Credit Suisse bonds in its largest buyback so far, reducing legacy debt to about $29 billion from roughly $90 billion at the time of the 2023 takeover. The bank had raised the cap on part of the tender twice and separately sold $6 billion of new senior debt. The transaction lowers interest expense and surplus funding, though UBS still faces an unresolved parliamentary debate over Swiss capital reforms.

Weaker credits did not receive the same reception. South East Water reconsidered a public bond sale after discussions with investors stalled over pricing. The utility has a £200 million liquidity backstop from King Street Capital intended to protect against a cash crunch previously projected for next August. Its gearing ratio of 66.5% exceeds the regulator’s target, and it recently paid a £30.5 million redress package following service failures and a credit downgrade. Investor demand existed, but not at terms the company was ready to accept.

Australian regulators were also testing the boundary between private credit and the regulated financial system. The prudential authority contacted banks and pension funds about exposure to collapsed property developer Bathla Group, whose creditors are owed about A$3.4 billion and are predominantly private lenders. Banks and regulated pension funds appeared to have limited direct exposure, and the Reserve Bank of Australia said it had not identified systemic stress. The inquiry nevertheless reflected concern that poor transparency and uncertain valuations could obscure the channels through which a private-credit failure spreads.

Senegal’s regional auction gave a more constructive signal after the sovereign announced plans for debt treatment. It raised 101 billion CFA francs, or $179 million, against an offer of 100 billion. Investors submitted 109 billion CFA francs of bids, and the government accepted almost all of them. The 5-year yield fell to 7.89% from 8.24% at the previous auction, while 1-year bills and 3-year bonds averaged 7.87% and 7.75%.

The result showed that Senegal’s plan had not triggered an immediate break in the regional market. The government intends to exclude CFA-franc debt and seek longer maturities and lower interest rates on external obligations under the G20 Common Framework. That distinction preserved local demand for now, but it also concentrates the eventual negotiation on international creditors after undisclosed borrowing led the IMF to suspend a $1.8 billion facility.

## Forward Market Significance

The Sept. 16 Fed decision, economic projections and Warsh press conference are the dominant test. A quarter-point increase is the market’s expected outcome after core CPI rose 0.3% and household inflation expectations increased. The larger question is whether policymakers describe the move as a limited reversal of earlier easing or the beginning of a longer campaign. Friday’s flatter curve and lower breakevens show that investors currently expect restraint to contain inflation; guidance implying substantially more tightening could lift real yields, while a hold would test the Fed’s credibility at the long end.

August retail sales arrive before the decision on Sept. 16. Expectations center on a 0.9% monthly rebound after a 0.6% decline, although available forecasts vary. Import and export prices are due at the same time. Retail demand will help determine whether higher prices are being absorbed by a resilient consumer or are eroding real spending, while import prices will show more directly how tariffs, energy and currency movements are entering U.S. costs.

Treasury supply presents a separate duration test. A 20-year auction is scheduled for Sept. 15 after a previous result of 5.204%, followed by a 10-year TIPS auction on Sept. 17 after a previous 2.438% real yield. The nominal sale will show whether demand remains firm with the 10-year Treasury near 5%; the inflation-protected sale will test appetite after the 10-year real yield rose to 2.596% and breakevens fell.

Oil may move those markets before the scheduled data. Saudi Arabia’s export inventories were estimated to cover five to seven days while the East-West pipeline remains offline. Partial pumping would reduce the immediate threat; a repair lasting five to six weeks could remove as much as 4% of global supply. The postponement of Gulf-Iran talks and new attacks around Hormuz have already reversed Friday’s crude decline at the Asian opening.

The BOJ meeting on Sept. 17-18 is expected to deliver a 25-basis-point increase to 1.25%. With that step effectively priced, the relevant test is whether Ueda validates a faster sequence while preserving flexibility over the terminal rate. A signal consistent with quarterly increases would support the yen and JGB yields and could accelerate the redirection of Japanese savings toward domestic bonds. A routine increase with cautious guidance would challenge the survey consensus for another move by January.

The Bank of England decision on Sept. 17 follows UK labor and inflation data. Most economists expect no immediate change, but July’s 0.4% GDP gain and the renewed energy shock have raised the probability of action by November. The annual announcement on the pace of gilt-balance-sheet reduction will matter alongside the policy rate because long-dated borrowing costs are already close to multidecade highs.

India’s local market must absorb the RBI’s 1 trillion-rupee bond-sale announcement when trading resumes. The first sale on Sept. 17 targets maturities from 2029 to 2032. The yield response will show whether removing record surplus liquidity merely restores the policy signal or forces a more disruptive repricing in the short and intermediate sectors.

Housing starts, permits and jobless claims arrive Sept. 17, followed by August industrial production on Sept. 18. Initial claims are expected to remain close to 209,000 after 206,000, while housing starts are expected to rebound from July’s decline. A combination of low layoffs and resilient production would reinforce the Fed’s ability to prioritize inflation. A broader weakening would make the duration and communication of any tightening cycle more consequential than the first increase itself.

The combination left Chair Kevin Warsh with less room to justify a September hold.

The IEA projected a 5.7 million-barrel-a-day contraction in 2026 supply, inventories were at their lowest since 2023, and refining and shipping constraints kept diesel pressure elevated. Demand destruction may eventually restrain prices, but only through weaker real growth.

ECB officials also signaled that persistent energy pressure could require mildly restrictive policy, while strong UK growth strengthened the case for eventual tightening. Russia paused easing, whereas softer Brazilian inflation preserved room for another rate cut.

section_summaries.section_title: India Turns a Liquidity Warning Into Bond Supply
section_summaries.summary: The RBI moved from warning about excess liquidity to announcing 1 trillion rupees of outright bond sales in three tranches beginning Sept. 17. Its first operation targets 2029-2032 maturities, adding supply where surplus bank cash had most distorted pricing. The action tightens financial conditions before the Oct. 7 policy decision as higher oil also threatens inflation, growth and the currency.

section_summaries.market_read: Open capital markets are rewarding structure, optionality and issuer quality rather than offering uniformly cheap funding.
section_summaries.section_title: Fiscal Stress and Credit Supply Produce Uneven Relative Value
section_summaries.summary: The U.S. deficit reached $1.97 trillion in the first 11 months of fiscal 2026, with net interest expense at $1 trillion, reinforcing structural pressure on long yields. In France, covered bonds yielded almost 30 basis points less than 10-year sovereign debt as fiscal stress weakened the government benchmark. Credit remained open but selective: AI-related convertible issuance surged, strong bank borrowers found demand, and weaker issuers faced resistance on price.

The Sept. 16 Fed decision is the dominant test of whether the expected increase is framed as a limited response or a longer campaign. Oil-supply disruptions could challenge Friday’s decline in breakevens before then, while the BOJ meeting will test expectations for a faster tightening cadence. Treasury auctions, U.S. activity data and India’s bond sales provide additional checks on duration demand and the transmission of tighter policy.

overall_summary.headline: Hotter core inflation lifts front-end yields as long Treasuries hold firm
overall_summary.session_narrative:
The 2-year Treasury yield rose 3.9 basis points to 4.626%, the 10-year edged 0.4 basis point higher to 4.968%, and the 30-year fell 1.3 basis points to 5.354%. The curve flattened as August core CPI increased 0.3%, above the 0.2% forecast, lifting the implied probability of a September Fed increase to around 90% and leaving two moves fully priced by year-end.

The market treated the release as a case for near-term restraint rather than evidence of unanchored long-run inflation. The 10-year real yield rose 4.9 basis points to 2.596%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 4.5 basis points to 2.372%. Oil’s retreat during the U.S. session helped long Treasuries recover, although crude still recorded a weekly gain of more than 8.5% and physical supply risks remained unresolved.

Household data made the policy choice less comfortable: consumer sentiment fell to 47.8, 1-year inflation expectations rose to 4.6%, and the 5-year measure increased to 3.4%. Even so, equities advanced, volatility declined and credit spreads tightened modestly, indicating a repricing of policy and real discount rates rather than broad funding stress.
